scenes.spoken: Who may see what? Seven models answer it, each from a different angle. Qadamar combines them in one decision.
Role-based access: rights follow the job. An analyst role, a finance role. Simple, but a role alone knows nothing about the record.
Attribute-based access: rules read the person, the record and its content. A financial amount is masked for anyone without the finance role.
Context-based access: same person, different situation. Off the trusted network, without recent M F A, or outside the grant window, access narrows. A missing signal fails closed.
Relations give a reason to know: the clinician who treats a patient. They form a graph, and every answer carries its path. A relation never lifts a clearance.
Bell La Padula, nineteen seventy-three, for confidentiality: no read up, no write down. Secrets never flow to a lower level.
Biba, nineteen seventy-seven, mirrors it for integrity: no write up. Less trusted data cannot corrupt more trusted data.
Clark Wilson, nineteen eighty-seven, for business integrity: sensitive changes run only through certified commands, with separation of duty and a single-use token.

Every request runs them in one fixed order: roles, the mandatory models, need-to-know, attributes, context, then certified commands and separation of duty. No tenant rule can reorder them or switch them off. One deny stops the request.
These are the models classified defence systems were built on. Qadamar brings them together in one self-hosted engine.
